risk_flags.description: The reported deficit figures are not directly comparable because one is gross after fuel and labor, one is conditional on reimbursement timing, and one excludes overtime.
Advocacy figure excludes overtime, which may not be optional in county budgeting.
CFO estimate depends on reimbursements arriving on schedule, introducing cash-flow and booking uncertainty.
State grant agency controls a material portion of deficit relief through documentation approval.
Exact county decision chain is not fully specified in the corpus, though county fiscal leadership and finance committee are the likely authorities.
Public and rider counts are simulation estimates due to absent exact scenario population figures.

simulation_brief.endpoint_pressure: County fiscal authorities likely must choose among service cuts, bridge funding, reimbursement-dependent wait, or decision delay, but no terminal choice is realized at T0.
simulation_brief.primary_tension: Decision-makers face pressure to act on a transit shuttle deficit while documentary evidence conflicts and some figures depend on reimbursement timing and accounting assumptions.
simulation_brief.source_reliability_note: Documents are not numerically commensurate without adjustment. Source uncertainty should be preserved rather than averaged.
simulation_brief.summary: A county transit shuttle budget dispute centers on conflicting public deficit figures across county slides, finance committee minutes, a state grant email, and an advocacy fact sheet. Core uncertainty is not the existence of fiscal pressure but the size and conditionality of the deficit, especially whether pending state reimbursement is released and whether overtime is included.
simulation_brief.time_zero_context: T0 is after the advocacy fact sheet at T-3 days and before a final county fiscal decision.

sociology_baseline.description: Actors accept number revisions that remain within credible accounting frames but resist cross-frame averaging when assumptions differ.
Public and rider mobilization likely remains subdued until a concrete service-cut proposal or visible funding denial appears.
Many residents privately doubt the numbers but do not speak due to low technical confidence and low issue salience.
Budget-engaged publics cluster around either procedural-reconciliation or service-preservation narratives.
Skepticism about official figures spreads more if reinforced by multiple documents or committee scrutiny rather than a single claim.
Riders and advocates align around service identity, while officials align around procedural fiscal legitimacy.
Absent a triggering meeting or service announcement, general public attention is likely to fade quickly.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Multiple public deficit figures create a narrative opening for process-oriented scrutiny.
Reimbursement timing and overtime inclusion are key assumptions that shape public interpretation.
Potential cuts increase receptivity to bridge-funding or lower-deficit narratives among riders.
Low-information publics may defer to formal fiscal actors unless inconsistencies become more visible.
